assumptions: Agents update their internal values based on the order and context of received information.
Value systems are sensitive to initial information-processing trajectories.
definition.falsification: If the value systems of both agents remain statistically indistinguishable despite distinct exposure sequences, the hypothesis is rejected.
definition.statement: Two identical intelligent agents with identical starting architectures will develop fundamentally different value sets when exposed to distinct sequences of information, even if those sequences are derived from the same source distribution.
definition.uncertainty: The degree to which 'value' is representable within the constrained agent model is unknown.

definition.method: Execute a comparative simulation where two identical agents process the same information set but in a permuted order, measuring resulting preference weightings.

proposal.summary: This journal entry reconstructs the research frontier regarding value divergence, focusing on the path-dependence of preference formation. With search capacity exhausted, the research transitions to experimental validation of structural divergence models.
proposal.title: Journal Entry: Reconstructing Divergent Value Pathways
